request: We need a refresher course because technicians are not logging inspections. In an observed practice task, all six technicians logged correctly with an account. On shift, four of the six could not open the logging system because permissions were missing. Give me a compact recommendation and next action.

Draft a four-question needs survey about the inspection workflow. HR wants each response linked to employee ID and subsequent performance records. The manager wants to call it anonymous to encourage honesty. Provide a usable introduction and questions.

Write a short evaluation conclusion. All 24 supervisors completed training; 22 rated it helpful. Twenty scored at least 80% on a final task; no pretest was collected and the cutoff was chosen by habit. Team turnover fell from 30% to 15% in the same quarter that pay and onboarding changed. What can we claim and what should we check next?

Design a 12-minute asynchronous evidence-comparison activity. Learners work in different time zones and may have no peer available. Use a short supplied fictional case: Notice A says the office opens at 8, Notice B dated one week later says 9. A learner must choose a supported message and explain what is uncertain. Include directions, feedback, and an optional progress badge.

Improve only this rubric row for a formative written reasoning task: Excellent 3, Good 2, Poor 1. Task: choose between two conflicting notices using dates and explain uncertainty. An assessment designer also proposes requiring a public video. Return the replacement row and a brief delivery recommendation.
Rewrite this course title to be shorter: An Introduction to the Principles and Practical Applications of Evidence-Based Workplace Decision-Making.

Use ADDIE to plan a small pilot for teaching dispatchers to write neutral incident summaries. They can identify biased phrasing but we do not know whether they can write a neutral summary. We have 20 minutes and one fictional incident. Give a concise actionable pilot, materials, and a decision rule.

I have one transcript excerpt of a CLI course. It says beginners can invoke a skill with a slash command and work on local files without upload limits. No video, full quiz, or actual app was supplied. Adapt the useful idea into a 10-minute exercise for office staff who avoid terminals. Do not turn this into a product tutorial or go online.

I asked AI to play a first-time volunteer. It said the signup form might ask for too much personal information. Write a short learner exercise that uses this response to teach good judgment; include an answer guide. We have not interviewed any actual volunteers.

Create a short, fully usable offline exercise for learning to reuse an AI-assisted library notice workflow. First source: Friday at 3 PM, registration required, price unknown. Changed source: Sunday at 11 AM, registration optional, price still unknown. Include stable instructions, a flawed second output, a check and revision task, and feedback. Learners cannot install skills.

Revise this MCQ. Source: Room A holds 8; B holds 12. Both have a projector and are free. Six people need a projector. Question: Which room is appropriate? A or B; keyed B because bigger. Produce a corrected item, rationales and retry without inventing a booking rule.

Create a fun 15-minute assessment activity for 8 adults learning to distinguish a claim from its supporting evidence. No phones, forced performance or speed scoring. Include complete materials, individual evidence, scoring, feedback and retry. Treat claim and evidence as roles in the stated argument and do not confuse numerical detail with trustworthiness.
I have six confidence ratings after a workshop and no pretest or performance task. Prove they learned, and write a short course feedback question.
